posts.description:
Node says my ES module is "a CommonJS module" even though package.json has "type": "module"

A small ES-modules-only library (package.json has "type": "module", the code uses export/import, tests run with node --test). `npm test` fails before any test runs:
SyntaxError: Named export 'slugify' not found. The requested module '../src/index.js' is a CommonJS module, which may not support all module.exports as named exports.
Tried: (1) checking that the root package.json really says "type": "module" - it does; (2) Node's own suggestion, `import pkg from '../src/index.js'; const { slugify } = pkg;` - that only changes the error to SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export', because Node then runs the file as CommonJS; (3) reinstalling node_modules and switching Node versions - no change, because nothing was wrong with the install. Renaming everything to .mjs or rewriting it as CommonJS would hide the problem but breaks the published import paths.
posts.value: The error points at the import line and at the root package.json, but Node decides ESM vs CommonJS from the NEAREST package.json, and a leftover one deeper in the tree was overriding the root.
posts.solution: Look for another package.json between the file and the project root: `find . -name package.json -not -path '*/node_modules/*'`. Here src/package.json (left over from an old dual CommonJS/ESM build) contained "type": "commonjs". For every .js file, Node uses the "type" of the closest package.json above it, so everything in src/ was loaded as CommonJS even though the root says "module". Fix: delete src/package.json (or change it to "type": "module"), then rerun `npm test`. Why it works: with no closer package.json, src/*.js falls back to the root's "type": "module", so the export statements are parsed as ESM and the named imports resolve. No code changes are needed.

posts.description:
pytest ignores pythonpath = ["src"] in pyproject.toml: ModuleNotFoundError for my src-layout package

A src-layout project (the package is in src/shopcart/). pyproject.toml has [tool.pytest.ini_options] with pythonpath = ["src"] and testpaths = ["tests"], which should put src/ on sys.path. But `python -m pytest` stops during collection:
ImportError while importing test module 'tests/test_cart.py'.
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'shopcart'
ERROR tests/test_cart.py
Interrupted: 1 error during collection
Tried: (1) adding an empty tests/__init__.py - same error; (2) adding tests/conftest.py - same error; (3) running `pytest tests` instead of `python -m pytest` - same error; (4) checking the pytest version (9.x, so the pythonpath setting is supported). `pip install -e .` or PYTHONPATH=src would hide it, but the project must run from a plain checkout, and nobody knows why the pyproject.toml setting is ignored.
posts.value: Open question: the configuration looks right but pytest acts as if it is not there, so the real cause is still unknown.

posts.description:
Windows: PermissionError [WinError 32] when moving a SQLite file after using it, even after closing the connection

A nightly job exports a POS terminal's SQLite database, then moves the .db file (and the terminal's .log) into an archive folder with os.replace. On Windows `python -m unittest` fails at the move every time:
PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: '...\pos-17.db' -> '...\archive\2026-10-24\pos-17.db'
Linux CI is green. Tried: (1) closing the connection used in `with sqlite3.connect(db) as con:` - same error; (2) removing the functools.lru_cache around the connect helper - same error; (3) gc.collect() and a retry loop with sleep before os.replace - same error; (4) shutil.move instead of os.replace - same error, because it falls back to copy + delete. Copying and leaving the original is not allowed. Each fix looked right but the error never changed.
posts.value: On Windows an open handle blocks moving or deleting a file, and here several different objects each keep the file open. Every one must be closed, so each single correct fix gives exactly the same error. Find every holder, not just the first.
posts.solution: List everything that can still hold the file when os.replace runs, and close each one explicitly (don't rely on garbage collection): (1) `with sqlite3.connect(db) as con:` only commits or rolls back, it does NOT close; use `with contextlib.closing(sqlite3.connect(db)) as con, con:` or call con.close(). (2) A connection cached with functools.lru_cache lives forever; open it per call and close it in try/finally. Just removing the cache is not enough when an exception is stored somewhere (here stats.warnings keeps the OperationalError): its traceback keeps the function's frame, and so the connection, alive. (3) A generator that was only partly read (itertools.islice(iter_sales(db), 3)) is paused inside its `with closing(...)` block, so its connection is still open; call gen.close() after taking the rows, or use a separate LIMIT query. (4) The same error then shows up for the .log file: a logging.FileHandler on it stays open because loggers are global and live forever; close and remove the handler (handler.close(); logger.removeHandler(handler)) before moving the log. Then `python -m unittest` passes. Why it works: Windows refuses to rename a file while any handle is open, and these four objects were the only handles.
